sentences.text: 2. Parties to the appeal are referred with their ranks as assigned in the Trial Court for the sake of convenience.

3. The factual matrix leading to the case of prosecution can be stated in nutshell to the effect that accused No.1 is the husband of deceased Renukamma and their marriage was performed about six years back.

Out of the wed lock, they have The State Of Karnataka vs Gopal on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2053053/

Accused No.2 was ill advicing her son and at her instance accused CRL.A. No.231 OF 2017 No.1 use to ill-treat deceased Renukamma.
About one month back, the marriage of her brother-in-law Ramesh was fixed with the girl from her village.
The deceased Renukamma was opposing for the said alliance, since she also belongs to the same village.

On such objection of deceased Renukamma,
there were to be quarrel between deceased Renukamma and accused.
3(a). On the eve of Ugadi festival deceased Renukamma and accused No.1 had came to Hosapalya and deceased Renukamma has picked up quarrel with accused No.1.
He informed over phone to her sister Mangala and asked to advice deceased Renukamma.
Therefore, deceased Renukamma was taken to her parental house.
After Ugadi festival on 10.04.2008 Mangala along with deceased Renukamma went to the house of accused No.1 for leaving her sister.
However, accused No.1 asked Mangala to leave Renukamma in the house at Hosapalya.
On the same day at 12.30 p.m. Mangala left deceased Renukamma in the house of accused No.1 at Hosapalya.
The deceased Renukamma CRL.A. No.231 OF 2017 was being insisted to stay in the village itself.

3(b). On 11.04.2008 at about 10.30 a.m. some unknown person of Hosapalya informed Mangala about her sister Renukamma having committed suicide by hanging herself in the house of accused No.1 at Hosapalya.
It is alleged that sister of complainant PW.1 Mangala on account of ill-treatment and harassment by both the accused, she committed suicide and her death has occurred within seven years of marriage.

On these allegations made in the complaint the Investigating Officer has carried out the investigation and on completion of investigation filed charge sheet under Sections 498-A and 306 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter for brevity referred to as `the IPC').
4.
In response to the summons accused have appeared through their counsel.
The Trial Court on being Prima facie satisfied of the charge sheet materials framed charge against accused for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A and 306 of IPC.

The Trial Court has framed CRL.A.
No.231 OF 2017 additional charge on 25.11.2014 for the offence punishable under Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (hereinafter for brevity referred to as "D.P.Act") and also under Section 304-B of IPC.

3 7. Appellant/State challenging the judgment of acquittal of accused Nos.1 and 2 contended that the Trial Court has not properly appreciated the evidence of PWs.1 to 4 in the light of complaint allegations Ex.P.1.
The fact that deceased Renukamma has committed suicide in the house of accused No.1 at Hosapalya within seven years of marriage has not been disputed by the accused.

The prosecution has placed on record sufficient material evidence in the form of oral testimony of PWs.1 to 4 to prove that deceased Renukamma was subjected to physical and mental cruelty on demand of money to get a house at Puttenahalli on lease.
PW.18 Asha Parveen Tahasildar, Executive Magistrate while drawing inquest panchanama Ex.P.9 found death note inside the bra worn by deceased Renukamma Ex.P.2.
PW.1 Mangala handed over another death note of deceased Renukamma which was found in her diary Ex.P.3.
The admitted writings of deceased Renukamma in the note book was also produced.
The documents at Exs.P.2 to 4 were subjected to hand writing expert opinion.

PW.14 Zeenath M, FSL CRL.A. No.231 OF 2017 officer has examined Exs.P.2 to 4 and given report Ex.P.13 holding that the writings found in the death note Exs.P.2 and 3 match with the writing found in Ex.P.4 and by the said evidence on record the prosecution has proved that it is only deceased Renukamma has written the death note Exs.P.2 and 3.
The said evidence placed on record by the prosecution has not been properly appreciated.
In the light of evidence of material witnesses of the prosecution in the form of PWs.1 to 4.

The oral testimony of PW.18 Asha Parveen, Tahsildar conducted inquest panchanama Ex.P.9 and the evidence of Investigating Officer PW.12 R.G.Ravikumar and PW.13 B.Raju corroborated the oral testimony of PWs.1 to 4.
The finding recorded by Trial Court are contrary to law and evidence on record.
Therefore, prayed for allowing the appeal and to set aside the judgment of Trial Court, consequently to convict the accused for the offences alleged against them.

10. After hearing both sides and on perusal of the Trial Court records, the following points arise for consideration:
1) Whether the prosecution has proved beyond all reasonable doubt that accused Nos.1 and 2 being the husband and mother-in-law of deceased Renukamma have ill-treated and harassed deceased Renukamma.
Further subjected her to physical and mental cruelty, thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 498-A of IPC?

2) Whether the prosecution further has proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on account of such ill-treatment and harassment by accused on 11.04.2008 on 10.30 a.m. deceased Renukamma committed suicide in the house of accused at Hosapalya village by hanging herself to the iron hook of the house due to intolerable treatment of accused and on account of such abetment committed suicide, thereby committed an offence The State Of Karnataka vs Gopal on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2053053/
4 - 10 - CRL.A. No.231 OF 2017 punishable under Section 306 of IPC?

3) Whether the prosecution further has proved beyond all reasonable doubt that deceased Renukamma due to intolerable dowry harassment on 11.04.2008 at 10.30 a.m. in the house of accused at Hosapalya committed suicide by hanging herself to iron hook of the roof of house within seven years of her marriage and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 306-B of IPC?

4) Whether the prosecution further has proved beyond all reasonable doubt that accused Nos.1 and 2 being the husband and mother in law of deceased Renukamma started demanding additional dowry for mortgaging house at Puttenahalli on lease and harassed her to meet such demand thereby committed an offence punishable Section 4 of D.P.Act?
5) Whether the judgment of Trial Court requires any interference by this Court?

The prosecution to prove that deceased Renukamma was subjected to physical and mental cruelty on demand of money for getting house on lease at Puttenahalli and on account of continuous ill-treatment and harassment, the deceased Renukamma committed suicide in the house of accused at Hosapalya, relies on the evidence of PW.1 Mangala, PW.2 Nagesh, PW.3 Puttaiah, PW.4 Nagamma who are the younger sister, younger brother, uncle and mother of deceased Renukamma.
The prosecution to prove the recovery of two pieces of rope seized under spot panchanama Ex.P.7 relied on the evidence of PW.8 Honnappa, PW.10 Thammaiah and PW.11 Harshad.

The prosecution to prove the unnatural death of deceased Renukamma in the house of accused at Hosapalya relies on the evidence of PW.18 Asha Parveen,Tahsildar who has conducted inquest panchanama Ex.P.9 and the independent panch witness PW.10 Thammaiah.
The said evidence is sought to be corroborated by the evidence of PW.7 Dr.Prakash who has conducted autopsy of deceased Renukamma and issued - 12 - CRL.A. No.231 OF 2017 post mortem report Ex.P.6.

The prosecution to prove the writings of deceased Renukamma in death note Exs.P.2 and P.3 and in notebook Ex.P.4 and subjected the said documents to FSL examination relies on the evidence of PW.14 Zeenath M.

The hand writing expert PW.14 Zeenath M, examined the documents at Exs.P.1 to 4 and given report Ex.P.13 and opined that the writings found in the death note Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.3 are that of deceased Renukamma.

The death of deceased Renukamma has occurred within seven years of her marriage and to prove the said fact relied on the oral testimony of PWs.1 to 4 and the said evidence is sought to be corroborated by the evidence of Investigating Officer PW.12 R.G.Ravikumar and PW.13 B.Raju.

Per contra the learned counsel for respondents has argued that in view of the admission of PWs.1 to 4 during the course of their cross-examination dislodges the case of prosecution as alleged in the complaint Ex.P.1.

It has been admitted by PW.1 Mangala, PW.2 Nagesh and PW.4 Nagamma that accused No.1 by giving `1,50,000/- got the house on lease and in which he was residing with his wife and son, therefore, there is no question of accused demanding money for getting the house on lease.

The death note at Ex.P.3 was alleged to have been produced by PW.1 Mangala after six months of the incident and in view of the admission of PW.14 Zeenath.M during the course of her cross-examination makes her evidence unreliable to prove the alleged death note of deceased Renukamma Exs.P.2 and 3.

The mere fact that deceased Renukamma committed suicide in the house of accused at Hosapalya within a period of seven years of her marriage - 15 - CRL.A. No.231 OF 2017 cannot be said as sufficient evidence to hold that it is a case of dowry death and deceased Renukamma committed suicide on account of alleged ill-treatment and harassment by accused.

The other attending circumstances brought on record during cross examination of prosecution witnesses will have to be appreciated while deciding as to whether death of Renukamma is a dowry death and she committed suicide in the house of accused at Hosapalya due to alleged demand of dowry as claimed by PWs.1 to 4 during the course of their evidence.

6 properly appreciated the evidence on record and no interference of this Court is required.
14.

Before proceeding further in analysing the evidence led in the matter, it is to be borne in mind that it is an appeal against the judgment of acquittal of the accused for the alleged offence punishable under Sections 498-A and 306 of IPC.
Therefore, the accused has primarily the double benefit.
Firstly, the presumption under law that, unless the guilt is proved, the accused has to be treated as innocent in the alleged crime.

Secondly,
- 16 - CRL.A. No.231 OF 2017 the accused is already enjoying the benefit of judgment of acquittal passed under the impugned judgment.
As such, bearing the same in mind, the evidence placed by the prosecution in the matter is required to be analysed.

(a) Our Hon'ble Apex Court, in its judgment in the case of Chandrappa and others -vs- State of Karnataka, reported in (2007) 4 Supreme Court Cases 415, while laying down the general principles regarding powers of the Appellate Court while dealing in an appeal against an order of acquittal, was pleased to observe at paragraph 42(4) and paragraph 42(5) as below:
" 42(4) An appellate court, however, must bear in mind that in case of acquittal, there is double presumption in favour of the accused.

sentences.text: Firstly, the presumption of innocence is available to him under the fundamental principle of criminal jurisprudence that every person shall be presumed to be innocent unless he is proved guilty by a competent court of law.
Secondly, the accused having secured his acquittal, the presumption of his innocence is further - 17 - CRL.A. No.231 OF 2017 reinforced, reaffirmed and strengthened by the trial court.
42(5) If two reasonable conclusions are possible on the basis of the evidence on record, the appellate court should not disturb the finding of acquittal recorded by the trial court."

(b) In the case of Sudershan Kumar -vs- State of Himachal Pradesh reported in (2014) 15 Supreme Court Cases 666, while referring to Chandrappa's case (supra), the Hon'ble Apex Court at Paragraph 31 of its Judgment was pleased to hold that, it is the cardinal principle in criminal jurisprudence that presumption of innocence of the accused is reinforced by an order of acquittal.

While dealing with an appeal against acquittal by invoking Section 378 Cr.P.C,
the - 18 - CRL.A. No.231 OF 2017 appellate Court has to consider whether the trial court's view can be termed as a possible one, particularly when evidence on record has been analysed.
The reason is that an order of acquittal adds up to the presumption of innocence in favour of the accused.
Thus, the appellate Court has to be relatively slow in reversing the order of the trial court rendering acquittal.
Therefore, the presumption in favour of the accused does not get weakened but only strengthened.
Such a double presumption that enures in favour of the accused has to be disturbed only by thorough scrutiny on the accepted legal parameters."

The above principle laid down by it in its previous case was reaffirmed by the Hon'ble Apex Court, in the case of Ravi Sharma -vs- State (Government of NCT of Delhi) and another reported in (2022) 8 Supreme Court Cases 536.

- 19 - CRL.A. No.231 OF 2017 "

sentences.text: In cases where a reversal of acquittal is sought, the Courts must keep in mind the presumption of innocence in favour of the accused, on grounds of it surviving to rigorous of full trial is strengthened and stands forfeited.
The prosecution then while still working under the same burden of proof, is required to discharge a more onerous responsibility to annual and reverse the forfeited presumption of innocence.
This fortification of the presumption of innocence has been held in a catena of judgment by this Court".

" Though it is true that as per Section 113A of the Evidence Act, when the question arises as to whether commission of suicide by a women had been abetted by her husband or any relative of her husband, and when it is shown that she had committed suicide within a period of seven years from the date of her marriage and that her husband or such relative of her husband had subjected her to cruelty, the Court can presume, having referred to the other circumstances, that such suicide has been abetted by her husband or such relative of her husband.

sentences.text: However, mere fact of commission of suicide by itself would not be sufficient for the - 51 - CRL.A. No.231 OF 2017 court to raise the presumption under Section 113A of the Evidence Act, and to hold the accused guilty of Section 306 IPC".

The Hon'ble Apex Court while referring its earlier judgments in para 9 has recorded finding in para 10 as under:
"In view of the above, it is quite clear that in order to bring the case within the purview of 'Abetment' under Section 107 IPC, there has to be an evidence with regard to the instigation, conspiracy or intentional aid on the part of the accused.

For the purpose proving the charge under Section 306 IPC, also there has to be an evidence with regard to the positive act on the part of the accused to instigate or aid to drive a person to commit suicide".

3 7. Appellant/State challenging the judgment of acquittal of accused Nos.1 and 2 contended that the Trial Court has not properly appreciated the evidence of PWs.1 to 4 in the light of complaint allegations Ex.P.1.
The fact that deceased Renukamma has committed suicide in the house of accused No.1 at Hosapalya within seven years of marriage has not been disputed by the accused.
The prosecution has placed on record sufficient material evidence in the form of oral testimony of PWs.1 to 4 to prove that deceased Renukamma was subjected to physical and mental cruelty on demand of money to get a house at Puttenahalli on lease.
Therefore, prayed for allowing the appeal and to set aside the judgment of Trial Court, consequently to convict the accused for the offences alleged against them.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The finding recorded by Trial Court are contrary to law and evidence on record.
The prosecution to prove that deceased Renukamma was subjected to physical and mental cruelty on demand of money for getting house on lease at Puttenahalli and on account of continuous ill-treatment and harassment, the deceased Renukamma committed suicide in the house of accused at Hosapalya, relies on the evidence of PW.1 Mangala, PW.2 Nagesh, PW.3 Puttaiah, PW.4 Nagamma who are the younger sister, younger brother, uncle and mother of deceased Renukamma.
Learned High Court Government Pleader apart from his oral arguments and to reiterate the same filed written argument contended that Trial Court has not properly appreciated the evidence of PWs.1 to 4 and their evidence is sufficient enough to prove the fact that deceased Renukamma was subjected to physical and - 13 - CRL.A. No.231 OF 2017 mental cruelty by demanding money.
The death note of deceased Renukamma Exs.P.2 and 3 with the writing Ex.P.4 were subjected to FSL examination and PW.14 Zeenath.
The proper custody and recovery of two death note Exs.P.2 and 3 with the writing of deceased Renukamma in Ex.P.4 has been established by the prosecution out of the evidence placed on record.
The Trial Court has not appreciated the said material evidence in the proper and appropriate manner - 14 - CRL.A. No.231 OF 2017 and as a result recorded improper finding in acquitting the accused for the charges levelled against them.
13.
The death note at Ex.P.3 was alleged to have been produced by PW.1 Mangala after six months of the incident and in view of the admission of PW.14 Zeenath.M during the course of her cross-examination makes her evidence unreliable to prove the alleged death note of deceased Renukamma Exs.P.2 and 3.
The mere fact that deceased Renukamma committed suicide in the house of accused at Hosapalya within a period of seven years of her marriage - 15 - CRL.A. No.231 OF 2017 cannot be said as sufficient evidence to hold that it is a case of dowry death and deceased Renukamma committed suicide on account of alleged ill-treatment and harassment by accused.
The other attending circumstances brought on record during cross examination of prosecution witnesses will have to be appreciated while deciding as to whether death of Renukamma is a dowry death and she committed suicide in the house of accused at Hosapalya due to alleged demand of dowry as claimed by PWs.1 to 4 during the course of their evidence.
The Trial Court has The State Of Karnataka vs Gopal on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2053053/
6 properly appreciated the evidence on record and no interference of this Court is required.
14.
Before proceeding further in analysing the evidence led in the matter, it is to be borne in mind that it is an appeal against the judgment of acquittal of the accused for the alleged offence punishable under Sections 498-A and 306 of IPC.
Therefore, the accused has primarily the double benefit.
Firstly, the presumption under law that, unless the guilt is proved, the accused has to be treated as innocent in the alleged crime.
Secondly,
- 16 - CRL.A. No.231 OF 2017 the accused is already enjoying the benefit of judgment of acquittal passed under the impugned judgment.
The prosecution is required to prove that deceased Renukamma was subjected to physical and mental cruelty on demand of dowry and her death was within seven years of her marriage and she committed suicide in the house of accused No.1 at Hosapalya due to alleged ill-treatment and harassment by accused on demand of dowry.
Thus, the prosecution by the evidence placed on record as referred above has failed to prove that deceased Renukamma was subjected to physical and mental cruelty on demand of dowry.
The death note Exs.P.2 and 3 and the writings of deceased Renukamma Ex.P.4 with proper custody and introducing them in the evidence has not been satisfactorily explained by the prosecution.
The standard of writing should be within five years for comparison.
In this context the Trial Court has rightly relied on the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Sohan Raj Sharma Vs. State of Haryana reported in 2008(2) Crimes-175 (SC) held as under:
" Sec.306 of IPC - more active role which can be described as instigating or aiding the doing of a thing is required before a person can be said to be abetting the commission of offence under Sec.306-If a victim committing suicide was hypersensitive to ordinary petulance,
- 50 - CRL.A. No.231 OF 2017 discord and differences in domestic life quite common to the society, such petulance discord and differences were not expected to induce an individual to commit suicide-The accused could not be found guilty of the charge of abetting suicide".
In view of the principles enunciated in these judgments, if the evidence of PW.1 Mangala, PW.2 Nagesha and PW.3 Nagamma are perused and appreciated with reference to the circumstances referred above then it - 52 - CRL.A. No.231 OF 2017 would go to show that their evidence finds short in proving accused having abated deceased Renukamma to commit suicide.
36. In view of the reasons recorded above it has been observed and held that the prosecution has failed to prove the demand of dowry and acceptance of the same before the marriage as deposed by PWs.1 to 4 during the course of their evidence and also demand of `50,000/- for getting house on lease at Puttenahalli, Bengaluru has not been proved by the prosecution.
Therefore it cannot be held that accused have committed offence under Section 304-B of IPC.
The Trial Court has rightly appreciated the evidence on record in holding that prosecution has failed to bring home guilt of accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
The said finding recorded by the Trial Court is based on the material evidence brought on record and the same does not warrant any interference by this Court.
opennyai_summary.issue:
10. After hearing both sides and on perusal of the Trial Court records, the following points arise for consideration:
1) Whether the prosecution has proved beyond all reasonable doubt that accused Nos.1 and 2 being the husband and mother-in-law of deceased Renukamma have ill-treated and harassed deceased Renukamma.
Further subjected her to physical and mental cruelty, thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 498-A of IPC?
2) Whether the prosecution further has proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on account of such ill-treatment and harassment by accused on 11.04.2008 on 10.30 a.m. deceased Renukamma committed suicide in the house of accused at Hosapalya village by hanging herself to the iron hook of the house due to intolerable treatment of accused and on account of such abetment committed suicide, thereby committed an offence The State Of Karnataka vs Gopal on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2053053/
4 - 10 - CRL.A. No.231 OF 2017 punishable under Section 306 of IPC?
3) Whether the prosecution further has proved beyond all reasonable doubt that deceased Renukamma due to intolerable dowry harassment on 11.04.2008 at 10.30 a.m. in the house of accused at Hosapalya committed suicide by hanging herself to iron hook of the roof of house within seven years of her marriage and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 306-B of IPC?
4) Whether the prosecution further has proved beyond all reasonable doubt that accused Nos.1 and 2 being the husband and mother in law of deceased Renukamma started demanding additional dowry for mortgaging house at Puttenahalli on lease and harassed her to meet such demand thereby committed an offence punishable Section 4 of D.P.Act?
5) Whether the judgment of Trial Court requires any interference by this Court?
opennyai_summary.decision:
Consequently, we proceed to pass the following:
- 53 - CRL.A. No.231 OF 2017 ORDER The Criminal Appeal stands dismissed as devoid of merits.
